_comment: wallspic.com, described 2026-10-16 from the site as it answers from this machine.
WHY THE HOMEPAGE LOOKED LIKE A JS SHELL AND IS NOT: the homepage carries 2 tags, both site
chrome. The album pages are a different story - each one publishes a schema.org ImageObject array in
a <script type="application/ld+json"> block: 30 items, each with description, datePublished,
contentUrl (the full-size file), fileFormat and a thumbnail object. That is the site declaring its
own pictures for crawlers, so this file reads the declaration instead of guessing at markup.
ROBOTS: /album/* is allowed; /upload, /search, /profile, /account and /api are disallowed under
every language prefix - so ask=false (the search box would be a disallowed path) and the album list
below is exactly what the site's own album page links, resolution albums first.
page: the album url, not a per-wallpaper page. The JSON-LD names no such page and the album page
links no per-item url we could read, so the origin written into the package points at the album the
picture was taken from rather than at an invented one.
key: the numeric id the file path repeats twice (/181827/181827-christmas_tree-...-3840x2160.jpg).
size: taken from the file name's own rung, so the card claims what the file actually is.
ext: fileFormat is image/jpeg today; the field is captured so a png album shows up honestly.
min_interval_ms 3000: one page is 30 pictures and 4 MB each; nothing here needs to be faster.
key: the numeric id the path repeats twice (/crops/7/2/8/1/8/181827/181827-<name>-3840x2160.jpg) -
the id is the last of the crop directories and again the file's own stem.

The file name's own parts are hyphen-separated, so the character class that eats it has to allow '-'; leaving it out matched 0 records while Python and the browser both show the page fine, which is the kind of failure that reads as 'the site changed'.
The CDN host in the pattern is img<N>.wallspic.com with one digit - if they ever add img10 the
record stops matching and the grid fails with 'no records', which is the loud kind of failure.
FILES HAVE NO LENGTH: img1.wallspic.com answers a Range probe with 200 and 'Transfer-Encoding:
chunked' and never a Content-Length; HEAD returns an empty body (measured 2026-10-16). So every
wallspic file goes down the one open-ended stream - ranges would buy nothing here. The first of
two attempts also died 9.5 s in without a single byte ('Connection closed'), which the hero retry
already covers; the 3.2 MB file that did arrive measured byte-identical to a fresh curl of the
same url.
